title: Traffic-split abort investigation and resilient rollback automation retro
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Summary: During a staggered traffic-split deployment (10% traffic to variant B), we observed a progressive increase in tail latency and a rise in semantic divergence for a subset of enterprise customers. The variant was eventually removed, but the automatic rollback did not trigger because the aggregation window and alert thresholds were misaligned with per-tenant latency spikes. This ticket captures the investigation, concrete runbook updates, telemetry improvements, and automation work to prevent recurrence.
timeline: 2026-02-08: Canary rollout started for model variant B at 10% global traffic split (policy: weighted routing by region)
2026-02-09 03:20 UTC: Ops observed subtle latency increase in region eu-west-1 (alerts not yet sensitive to per-tenant tails)
2026-02-09 04:10 UTC: Early escalation: SRE started live debug, noticed KV-cache warmup mismatch between control and canary pods for requests with long context
2026-02-09 04:25 UTC: Model outputs for some prompt prefixes showed semantic regression (higher hallucination score on internal eval), but non-actionable under global alert thresholds
2026-02-09 05:00 UTC: Manual abort of rollout initiated after product team flagged customer tickets from two enterprise orgs
2026-02-09 05:30 UTC: Variant B scaled down; rollback completed. Incident declared and postmortem started the following day
investigation_findings: Root cause 1: KV cache warmup and keyspace skew - canary pods served requests with cold cache for frequent long-prefix patterns used by affected customers, leading to higher compute and latency

Root cause 2: Telemetry aggregation mismatch - alerting relied on global p95 latency over 5m windows which smoothed per-tenant p99 spikes; per-customer traffic slice masking allowed regressions to persist

Root cause 3: Rollback automation gap - automatic rollback is gated by an aggregated SLA signal and required at least 10% absolute degradation over baseline; localized 40% p99 increase for specific customers did not meet global criteria
Contributing: Traffic-split sticky routing caused certain customers to be disproportionally routed to canary due to session affinity and sticky hash interaction
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Implement per-tenant and per-route SLI monitoring for canary traffic. Tradeoff: higher cardinality metrics and more storage/cost in observability stack

Decision: Introduce a lightweight synthetic preflight suite that runs the top 50 tenant prompt families against canary before traffic bump. Tradeoff: additional pre-deploy latency for canary creation, but prevents high-risk regresses
Decision: Reduce friction for faster manual aborts by adding an 'abort and snapshot' operator action in Console. Tradeoff: more surface area in UI that requires RBAC controls
Decision: Adjust auto-rollback thresholds to include a hysteresis window and per-tenant anomaly detectors rather than a single global delta. Tradeoff: more complex logic in rollout controller
runbook_changes: Add step: On early latency increase, run 'canary-kv-check' diagnostic to compare keyspace hit rates (playbook script: /runbooks/canary-kv-check.sh)
Add step: Query per-tenant p99 for past 10m and trigger immediate rollback if any customer exceeds 2x baseline p99 and shows >100 requests in window
Clarify owner: SRE retains primary incident owner for the first 30 minutes of a canary anomaly, Product on-call included for customer-impact assessment
Add post-abort checklist: collect canary pod traces, model deterministic seeds, and capture sampled request payloads to internal secure bucket for repro
telemetry_and_dashboards: Create Alert: 'Canary-p99-per-tenant' - fires if p99 > 2x baseline or absolute > 1200ms for 3/5 minutes
Instrument: track 'kv-cache-warmness' metric (ratio of cache hits for LRU keys used in last 24h) emitted by runtime agent
Add tracing tag: 'rollout_variant' to all spans so traces can be filtered by control/canary path in Jaeger
automation_tasks: ENG-116000: Extend rollout controller to accept 'per-tenant abort rules' and implement anomaly detector hook (owner: Miguel Santos, estimate: 5)
ENG-116101: Synthetic preflight runner service to exercise representative prompt families for candidate model variants (owner: Sarah Lin, estimate: 8)
ENG-116212: Add 'abort and snapshot' button to Console with RBAC checks and automatic audit log entry (owner: Ava Park, estimate: 3)
ENG-116323: Add end-to-end test to CI that simulates sticky routing and KV-cache coldstarts to validate rollback triggers (owner: Ethan Chen, estimate: 2)
prs_and_docs: Confluence: Incident writeup and long-form learnings (link: https://confluence.redwood.example/display/INFR/ENG-115412+Canary+Abort+Retro)
